opening.argument: The speaker presents BitClub as an accessible route to substantial, largely passive income, claiming "$ 6,000 net income" for a week without practically approaching the computer. He says such results are available to anyone who will develop a team, then describes qualification and earnings through a recruitment structure: becoming a builder requires earning 10.000$ in total and personally inviting five miners, each of whom must invite two more. The financial incentive is expressly tied to partners' activity, since "from every income of your partners, you get a reward." This is followed by an urgent instruction to take action and avoid losing income. The presentation therefore solicits participation in a paid, multi-level, recruitment-dependent earning structure, rather than describing or criticizing one.
